question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**biggest**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage refers to the US being the primary shareholder in the World Bank, and **biggest** fits well to describe the largest or most significant shareholder in the context of the World Bank.
 
• The word **biggest** aligns with the idea that the US holds the largest stake in the bank, which is a financial context.
 
• **Longest**, **tallest**, and **brightest** do not fit the context of describing financial stakes, as they refer to physical attributes or qualities, rather than the size or magnitude of a shareholding.
 
• **Biggest** is the most appropriate word to describe the largest shareholder in terms of financial influence or size of share in the bank.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The US is the (1) biggest__ shareholder in the World Bank and traditionally, the bank’s president has been a US citizen (2)_______ by Washington. Small island developing states have argued for moving the fund (3)_______ from a donor recipient model, with all their usual power imbalances, (4)______ a partnership founded on a shared commitment to protecting the planet. This will require partial or total (5)_______ of the World Bank. This is already happening under its new president, some argue. But hosting the fund within the bank would still give donor countries disproportionate influence.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Longest** refers to time or duration, which does not fit the financial context of being the largest shareholder in a bank.
 
• **Tallest** refers to height, which does not relate to shareholding or financial stakes in the context of the passage.
 
• **Brightest** is associated with light or intelligence, which is unrelated to the concept of shareholding or financial dominance in this passage.
